newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM to visit India to sign water deal.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM to visit India to sign water deal.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is expected to visit India next week to sign an agreement on sharing water from the Ganges river, one of her aides said on Wednesday.
"The prime minister is likely to leave for the Indian capital on December 9 for a four-day visit," he said.

Sharing the water from the Ganges has been a major irritant in relations between the neighbours since 1974 when India built the Farakka Barrage about 18 km (11 miles) from Bangladesh's northern border.
Dhaka says the barrage obstructs river flow during the dry season (December-May), depriving Bangladesh of its fair share of water.
Bangladesh has been insisting on a permanent agreement, but officials in Dhaka indicated that New Delhi preferred only a short-term accord.
The last agreement, under which Bangladesh received 35,000 cubic meters per second of Ganges water during the dry season, expired in 1988 and attempts until now to renew it failed.
Dhaka says more than 40 million people in north and northwest Bangladesh have faced gradual desertification of their land because of the Farakka dam.
